extracted.intended_audience: TV creators/producers, comedy writers, entertainment-industry readers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and behind-the-scenes principles for developing, adapting, and producing television comedy (here focused on adapting a British show and producing an adult-comedy series). Includes creative, cultural, casting, and technical considerations discussed at a festival panel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balancing comedic and medical elements
rubrics_metrics.description: The creators emphasized the importance of balancing the show’s comedic and medical elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hire subject-matter experts who understand storytelling — e.g., they hired a doctor who is also a television writer to help maintain medical accuracy while preserving comedic timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapting British comedy requires cultural translation
rubrics_metrics.description: There are cultural barriers between countries: what may be a joke to a Brit may make an American call HR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When adapting material, anticipate differences in humor and sensibilities; lean on original cast/creators as bridges and be mindful that certain jokes may need reworking for a new audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use authentic setting and research to inspire characters
rubrics_metrics.description: The show’s Maine setting was inspired by Tuccillo’s four-month trip and real people she met in the small town of Corea helped inspire characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground the adaptation in real-world research and local color to generate authentic character details and a believable sense of place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult original creators/actors to inform authenticity
rubrics_metrics.description: Martin Clunes (from the original Doc Martin) appeared and provided tips on character movements and medical practices; his involvement was called 'a blessing.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bringing original talent or creators onboard (cameos, consultation) can lend authenticity and reassure existing fans, and provide practical performance and factual insights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use table reads to test offensiveness and comedic beats
rubrics_metrics.description: At the table read, you get as many people as you can together to listen to the script. If there are things that are just too offensive to be funny, you’re met with dead silence in the room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize honest group table reads as a safety valve: silence or poor reaction signals material that may need rewrites; use diverse listeners to surface different reactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operate within given guidelines and exercise responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘We do try to be relatively responsible within the guidelines that we’re given,’ noting there are steps that prevent you from crossing the line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know network/platform standards and formal/informal boundaries, and build internal checkpoints (editorial, legal, creative) to avoid gratuitous or unacceptable content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft comedy that contains an underlying message
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Underneath all the absurdity, there’s a message,’ — the show’s humor is smart, winks at the audience, and may be layered so viewers either 'get it' or not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for comedic setups that also deliver thematic or emotional throughlines; smart satire/absurdity often works best when anchored by an intelligible message or point of view.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pushing the envelope can be intentional and polarizing
rubrics_metrics.description: Episodes like 'Roe v. Weed' (an abortion plot line) were described as 'ballsy' and 'pushing the envelope.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Risky subject matter can generate memorable storytelling but expect mixed reception; weigh creative intent against likely audience and stakeholder reactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical actor preparation for non-human characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Actors carried around stuffed bears to get comfortable with 'Ted' as a physical/imagined presence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use tactile rehearsal props and embodied techniques to help actors form relationships with non-human characters or puppets and to ground performances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage technology to solve performance and creative constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Season 2 development involved technology allowing fewer sensors on MacFarlane’s body for voicing the character and implementing AI to create a deepfake cameo of Bill Clinton.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt technical solutions (performance-capture improvements, AI/deepfakes, VFX) thoughtfully to reduce practical burdens and enable creative choices, while considering ethical/legal implications.
